title: Kahana vs Apple Books: A Stack for the Club, Not a Lifetime Catalog
excerpt: Apple Books is reading, catalogs, tracking, or ebook storefronts. Kahana is clubs and hubs around the books you actually read together.

metaDescription: Apple Books is reading, catalogs, tracking, or ebook storefronts. Kahana is clubs and hubs around the books you actually read together.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Roughly 10–14% share of the global ebook market, second only to Amazon (≈38%).
In the U.S., ≈10% market share, having overtaken Barnes & Noble for second place.
In Australia, around 30% of the ebook market.
In some analyses, ≈21% of sales and ≈11% of downloads, with Amazon dominating at 53–66%.

strengths.title: Seamless Apple ecosystem integration
strengths.detail: Native across iPhone, iPad, and Mac; syncs reading position, notes, and highlights via iCloud.

strengths.title: Unified ebooks + audiobooks
strengths.detail: One app for reading and listening; curated collections and charts across genres.

strengths.title: High-quality reading UX
strengths.detail: Attractive typography, page layouts, and accessibility features tuned for Apple devices.

strengths.title: Simple self-publishing tools
strengths.detail: Free tools like Pages to create EPUBs and publish to Apple Books, plus preferred partners for distribution.

weaknesses.title: Smaller catalog and share vs Amazon
weaknesses.detail: Significantly behind Kindle in global ebook share and title availability (typically ~10–14% vs Amazon’s ~38%).

weaknesses.title: iOS / macOS lock-in
weaknesses.detail: Best experience requires Apple devices; no native Apple Books app for Android or non-Apple e-readers.

weaknesses.title: In-app purchase friction
weaknesses.detail: Apple’s ~30% IAP cut can make competing bookstore apps less attractive and confuse users choosing reading apps.

weaknesses.title: Less community / social
weaknesses.detail: Focused on reading and discovery; lacks social reading or community depth on par with Goodreads or Wattpad.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Apple Books is reading, catalogs, tracking, or ebook storefronts. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Apple Books is the single destination to find, buy, and dive into audiobooks and ebooks.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Apple Books side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Apple Books you can use Ebook, Memberships, and Marketplaces as first-class product jobs. You need a dedicated reader, a giant store, or social tracking of everything you have ever read.

Using Kahana with Apple Books

You can use both. Apple Books keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the reader or tracker you already use. Put the Club pick, discussion questions, and related files on Kahana so the book is a shared library item, not only a private progress bar.
